structured_output.summary: Phased curve is a baseline-free sinusoid, not a transit; fit_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.59 is unphysical.
reasons: I disagree with the mechanical decision (proposed for submission). The all-sector figure tic146282462_1.21673.png shows no flat out-of-transit baseline in any of Sector 104, 3, 30 or 97: the binned flux falls smoothly from about +500 ppm at -12 h to a minimum near -3000 ppm at mid-transit and rises again symmetrically over the full +/-12 h window, and the phase-0.5 panel shows a broad brightening to about +2500 ppm, not a flat baseline. This is a continuous sinusoid at the 1.2168 d period (or a contact binary at twice it), not a planetary transit. The red transit model is visibly a poor match in every sector panel.

The transit fit is unphysical: fit_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.59 +/- 0.001 puts the companion at 1.59 stellar radii, essentially at the stellar surface; fit_duration_hours 6.728 is 23% of the 1.2168 d period, which is why step 9 raises the caution 'dip longer than a transit at this period'; and stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 0.305 shows the fit only matches the shape by making the star three times less dense than the TIC star (stellar_radius_solar_radii 2.38574). transit_grazing is False (fit_impact_parameter 0.029), so the shape is not explained by grazing geometry; it is the wrong model.

secondary_depth_ppm -1470 +/- 104 is a 14-sigma brightening at phase 0.5 (the earlier step-9 run in the record gave -2448 +/- 63 ppm). A planet cannot produce a negative secondary; a sinusoidal variation at the orbital period does exactly this. ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm -5543 is likewise large though poorly constrained (ellipsoidal_amplitude_error_ppm 4048).

The star is almost certainly a close binary or a tidally spun-up variable: gaia_non_single_star 2, gaia_ruwe 1.43, gaia_rv_variable True with gaia_rv_epoch_range_km_s 48.85 over gaia_rv_nb_transits 51 (gaia_rv_chisq_pvalue 0.0, gaia_rv_renormalised_gof 25.2), and gaia_vbroad_km_s 96.97. The step-9 upper limit gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.14 rests on gaia_rv_epoch_scatter_km_s 13.6 and gaia_rv_semi_amplitude_upper_limit_km_s 19.2, which conflicts with the 48.85 km/s epoch range and should not be relied on.

Depths are inconsistent across sectors and apertures in a way a fixed-depth transit does not produce: sector_depth_consistency_p_value 4.57e-05 (depth_ppm_by_sector S3 3630 +/- 180 vs S104 2649 +/- 113), and cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value 2.65e-159, with the S97 cutout depth rising from 10352 ppm at r1.5 to 18264 ppm at r3.0 (cutout_depth_ppm_by_sector_and_aperture). This is the behaviour of a variable-star amplitude that depends on detrending and aperture, and it matches the caution 'depths differ between sectors'.

The supporting checks do not rescue the candidate. pixel_verdict on target with joint_difference_image_snr 33.7, confirmed in all seven pixel figures (S3, S30, S97, S104, S105, S106, S107 each show the difference-image peak on TIC 146282462), only establishes that the variability originates on the target itself, which is consistent with the star being the variable. triceratops_verdict 'validated without imaging' with fpp_mean -4.796e-14 assumes a transit-shaped signal and is meaningless when the fitted a/R* of 1.59 is outside physical priors; its most_likely_scenario changed between runs (TP then DTP), and the negative FPP itself signals a numerically degenerate result.

planet_radius_earth_radii 13.25 +/- 0.61 is below the 22.4 Earth-radius stellar limit, but it comes from fit_depth_ppm 2982 under a transit model fitted to a non-transit shape (the search depth_ppm 842.8 differs from the fit by a factor 3.5), so it does not support a planet interpretation.

Holding is not warranted. exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are empty, so the drop is for astrophysical reasons, not duplication. unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 105 106 107 already appear in the step-9 cutout depths and the step-8 pixel checks and show the same aperture-dependent, baseline-free signal (S106 cutout depth rising from 4203 ppm at r1.5 to 5810 ppm at r3.0); more sectors cannot turn a sinusoid into a transit. This agrees with the earlier agent decision of 2026-10-17 recorded in the verification record, and the later step-9 reruns (e83ce09, 5980fd1) changed no value and added the long-duration caution.
